mechanism_narrative: The steady week-to-week decline in WORKPLACES intensity is translating into fewer discretionary daytime trips, so retail and recreation will continue rising relative to the last month as commuting activity rebounds into consumer visits.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -56.3 to -37.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES does not keep trending upward and RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the prior 28 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in RESIDENTIAL time from elevated levels indicates households are spending more time out of home, which should lift retail and recreation mobility within the next week as trips shift from home-based to destination-based activity.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15 points above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 24.6 to 14.9 while RETAIL_REC rose from -73.0 to -37.6
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above the trigger and RETAIL_REC does not improve within one week, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together, the same commuting flow produces more intermediate stopping and shopping opportunities, so retail and recreation should strengthen over the next two to four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved monotonically across the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES keep rising together but RETAIL_REC fails to increase relative to the previous four weeks, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp recovery in GROCERY_PHARM without a matching rise in PARKS marks a shift toward essential errand mobility, which should pull retail and recreation upward over the next two weeks as households resume bundled shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -15 while PARKS stays below 15
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -26.4 to -10.0 while PARKS moved from -20.9 to 19.3
failure_condition: If grocery mobility does not stay elevated or parks activity rises in a way that diverts trips away from retail, RETAIL_REC will not outperform the prior four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PARKS mobility signals warmer-weather discretionary outings, and that spillover should keep retail and recreation rising over the next four weeks as outdoor trips anchor nearby commercial visits.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns positive and stays above 10 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -20.9 to 19.3 over three weekly steps
failure_condition: If PARKS remains positive but RETAIL_REC does not continue improving over the next month, the seasonal spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent narrowing gap between TRANSIT and RESIDENTIAL implies more out-of-home activity and less staying home, which should raise retail and recreation within two weeks as discretionary travel replaces home-centered behavior.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -61.1 to -44.3 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 24.6 to 14.9
failure_condition: If the TRANSIT-RESIDENTIAL gap narrows but RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks, this mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: The recovery in GROCERY_PHARM above the mid-teens indicates relaxed access to local services, and once that threshold is crossed retail and recreation should keep climbing over the next four weeks through loosened movement constraints.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above -15 but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and TRANSIT both rise while WORKPLACES remain depressed, recreational travel substitutes for commuting and creates additional discretionary stopovers, producing a short-run lift in retail and recreation within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS turned positive and TRANSIT/WORKPLACES improved steadily across the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS and TRANSIT rise but WORKPLACES also normalize without a corresponding retail uplift, the substitution mechanism fails.
